summary: [standards, blast radius] What only a real S3 API shows is in no bound test: the CLI tests use the debug local-filesystem substitute, which keeps no metadata, so canon-size (the bomb limit), canon-stored-size (the HEAD size check) and the GET-time metadata read of verify_full_zst run only against InMemory. r2_tier_live.rs (skipped without MinIO, not extended for .zst) does put/probe/verify_full/list of a small blob only. I ran the real binary against a live MinIO container: metadata canon-sha256/canon-size/canon-stored-size round-trip; a 100 MB zeros bomb recorded as 405264 bytes stops at the limit (Altered, 0.07 s, RSS 42 MB); a flipped byte, a cut tail with a consistent and with a stale stored-size, and plain-only / zst-only / both-forms / neither digests give the answers the scenarios say (gate check and verify exit 0 for each single form, 1 for none; --full catches a corrupt plain object beside a good .zst that the HEAD cannot). No code defect; the live test should assert the bomb and stored-size paths so a release run keeps proving them.
